title: wt up --json
description: What a wt up run did. Printed by `wt up [<work>] --json` as the only thing on stdout, also when a handled SIGINT or SIGTERM ends the run. Schema 1: fields may be added and enumerations may gain values; nothing is renamed or removed. See docs/json.md.

schema.description: The major version: a new one only for a change that breaks readers.

schemaVersion.description: The full semantic version of this schema that the output follows: minor for an added field or enumeration value, patch for wording.

trunkSource.description: How trunk was determined, first match wins, from local refs alone (since 1.3.0): config — MAIN_BRANCH in the wt configuration file; originHead — refs/remotes/origin/HEAD; conventional — the first of development, main, master that exists locally or on origin (since 1.3.1; before, main, master, trunk, development, develop, ranked by where each exists); currentBranchGuess — no longer produced since 1.3.1: when nothing names trunk, detection fails and the repository reports noConfiguration. Null when trunk is.

onto.description: The trunk commit the run rebased onto, after its fetch; null when never determined.

trunkSync.description: What the run did to local trunk after its fetch: fast-forwarded to origin/<trunk> when safe, or why not. Null when it did not fetch.

outcome.description: done: every participant rebased, fastForwarded or skipped. refused: nothing changed, or error stopped the run first. partial: something changed and not everything finished. interrupted: a signal ended the run.

error.description: Why the run stopped before touching any participant.

recovery.description: For interrupted: the way back wt printed.

trunkSync.description: Local trunk against origin/<trunk>, and what was done about it. See docs/json.md.

local.description: Local trunk after the run (as found unless fast-forwarded); null when there is none.

remote.description: The origin/<trunk> commit compared with; null when there is none.

localAhead.description: Commits local trunk has that origin lacks, as found.

remoteAhead.description: Commits origin has that local trunk lacks, as found.

skippedReason.description: Why local trunk was left; null when fast-forwarded or with nothing to do.

result.description: rebased, fastForwarded, rebasedStepFailed, needsRecovery, handedOver and interrupted changed the branch or worktree; skipped, refused, notRun and restored left them as they were. fastForwarded (since 1.4.0): the branch was behind its own remote and has nothing to rebase at the remote's commit, so the run moved it there and that is all; after is that commit, pushCommand is null.

pushCommand.description: For rebased: the push, as an argv.

ownRemoteSync.description: Since 1.4.0: what the run found of a participant's own remote, the remote-tracking ref a push of its branch would replace, and what it did about it. See docs/json.md.

ref.description: The remote-tracking ref, as remote/branch; null only when no ref could be named.

state.description: As found, before anything moved; the states are those of ownRemote in wt status --json.

local.description: The branch as found, before any fast-forward: where wt sync undo puts it back.

remote.description: The remote commit compared with; null for none, gone and unknown.

localAhead.description: Commits only the branch had; null for none, gone and unknown.

remoteAhead.description: Commits only the remote had; null for none, gone and unknown.

fastForwarded.description: The run moved the branch from local to remote before rebasing it. It stays true as a record when the rebase after it was put back, which takes the branch back to local.

allowed.description: state is diverged and the run went on over it under --allow-diverged; false when the participant was refused for something else.

skippedReason.description: Why the own remote refuses the participant; null when it does not. diverged: --allow-diverged goes on. operation, dirty, session: behind, and it cannot be fast-forwarded. failed: the fast-forward itself did not go through; nothing of this participant was touched. fetchFailed: the branch's own remote could not be fetched, so the run could not look; trunk's fetch failing is the run's error instead.
